blueprint.metaDescription: Create professional AI images and videos with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro by ByteDance. Explore image generation, video generation, enterprise-ready proof, pricing, testimonials, and get started.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like an enterprise product landing page for a solution-aware audience evaluating advanced AI generation tools. The strongest conversion path is demo-booking, not immediate purchase, because the product is high-consideration and the provided pricing still routes to quote/demo intent. Since the visitor trusts logos most, the design should be logos-first with a prominent trust strip and restrained, premium visual treatment. The hero should be text-led and split, but only if the split is used for supporting proof or product-relevant media, not an empty form area. The page should remain dark-themed, modern, and credible, with balanced density to accommodate both product explanation and proof. A video gallery is important because Seedance is video-native and needs visual demonstration, while Seedream needs a clear feature stack to communicate image quality, fidelity, and multimodal editing. Overall, the experience should feel enterprise-ready, product-led, and optimized to move qualified visitors into a demo or quote request.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark full-bleed hero with generative output collage, precision-line grid, floating prompt-to-output cards, and a thin logo row integrated beneath the headline block
sections.designNote: Make the hero answer all quality-check questions immediately: this is ByteDance generative AI for professionals creating images and videos, and the next step is Get started. Keep the headline content-first but support it with premium output visuals and an above-the-fold logo proof line. Use strong spacing, mono heading typography, and a solid orange CTA button. Mobile CTA must be full-width.

Use 3-6 recognizable customer/enterprise logos in a static flex-wrap grid. Since actual logos are not provided, treat this as a clean logo strip placeholder only if real logos are available; otherwise replace with a slim metric strip. Keep this section compact and immediately after the hero to satisfy the logos-first trust strategy.

Use a two-stage product story rather than a generic SaaS feature grid. First spotlight Seedream 4.5 with tabs and a live preview panel for image generation, then invert the visual balance for Seedance 1.5 Pro with a media-led panel for video and audio synchronization. Because there are 5+ features, avoid a flat static grid; use tabs with preview and feature bullets inside the active panel. Alternate the left-right composition between the two product blocks to break rhythm.

Use testimonial-style proof cards because customer logos are not supplied in the input set beyond the trust requirement. Highlight industry-specific creative confidence: creative directors, video producers, art directors, and marketing managers. Keep the section visually lighter than the product blocks, with short quotes and strong attribution hierarchy.

Present two clear enterprise-ready plan cards, but avoid making pricing feel like a commodity grid. Emphasize the image and video model differences, then anchor each card with a single solid Get started CTA. Keep the pricing area more controlled and technical than promotional.

Use a compact testimonial carousel or 3-card row with stronger quote emphasis than decorative styling. Since there are 5 testimonials, a carousel or tightly spaced grid is appropriate. Keep this section visually calmer than pricing to create a credibility pause before conversion.

Use a centered high-focus conversion card. Keep the form minimal if fields are later added, but the primary CTA must always read Get started. This is the final action point and should feel decisive, premium, and enterprise-safe. Mobile CTA full-width.

Do not introduce a separate news or marquee section because the visual system and trust strategy are already satisfied by the hero logo row and proof blocks. End cleanly after the form to maintain conversion focus.

blueprint.designPersonality: A dark, technically precise AI studio for enterprise teams — minimal, confident, and output-first, with sharp typography, orange accents, strong logo proof, and a premium video gallery that signals production-grade generative quality.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use dark, cinematic product visuals with authentic AI-generated preview frames: image tiles, prompt-to-output comparisons, video thumbnails, audio waveform overlays, and enterprise workflow shells. Include a dedicated video gallery feel inside the product section with thumbnail cards, play badges, duration labels, and subtle motion framing. Logos should be the strongest trust layer. If real screenshots are missing, use polished CSS-based mockups with precise grid overlays, output cards, and media controls.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long, so a smaller hero size keeps it powerful without wrapping awkwardly in a dense technical layout.

colours.colourReason: Brand colors are locked to Techjockey’s palette: dark charcoal for the base with the official orange accent for CTAs and highlights. This preserves a distinct identity while still feeling premium and product-focused.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column hero with brand/logo placement, large headline, short supporting paragraph, and a compact bullet-benefit list. Visual emphasis is text-led rather than media-led, with strong top-left hierarchy and immediate CTA adjacency.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero-to-form lead capture flow followed by stacked product detail sections. The page uses a linear sales funnel rhythm: awareness, conversion form, then feature deep-dives with repeated CTA opportunities.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Simple rectangular content cards and form panel styling. The visual language is utilitarian and enterprise-oriented, favoring clean containers, clear borders or subtle separation, and limited decorative treatment.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero as a high-priority action; secondary conversion is handled through a lead form card. Product sections can include their own CTA when needed, but the overall pattern emphasizes one dominant conversion target per stage.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing-led module in the reference structure. If introduced, pricing should follow the same lead-generation pattern: concise plan cards, clear compare hierarchy, and CTA routed to demo/request flow.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference structure. Recommended footer mode for this pattern is minimal utility footer with links, compliance, and contact support, keeping conversion content above the fold and primary sections uncluttered.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Logo-first banner with little to no hero illustration. Media usage is restrained and functional; when present, it should support trust or brand recognition rather than compete with the headline.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Stacked feature sections with clear section labels, large headline, descriptive paragraph, and a feature list. Each section should read as a self-contained module with progressive disclosure from summary to bullet-level benefits.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-capture card placed directly after the hero. Form treatment is prominent, boxed, and conversion-focused, with supporting title text above and hidden metadata inputs underneath for tracking and routing.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, enterprise-style presentation with no visible motion system in the reference markup. Any motion should remain subtle, functional, and limited to standard page transitions or form interactions.
componentPatterns: Benefit bullet list with icon ticks
designNotes: Use a conversion-first layout with minimal ornamentation.
Keep hierarchy crisp: logo, headline, subheadline, benefits, CTA, then form.
Prefer stacked sections over complex navigation patterns.
Use bold section headers and short, scannable feature bullets.
Maintain generous whitespace and clear separation between modules.
If media is added, keep it secondary to the CTA and value proposition.
Avoid carousel-heavy or interaction-heavy patterns for this type of page.
Use repeated but restrained CTAs to support a long-form lead-gen journey.
